trust_decision.summary: The shared Lucene filter-string escaper emitLuceneString must also backslash-escape tab, newline, carriage return and U+3000 so a metadata filter key cannot terminate its field term and start a new clause in the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/GemFire query string; the decision is made in spring-ai-vector-store's AbstractFilterExpressionConverter, which all three store converters call.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names only Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and GemFire, so an engineer looks first at those three store converters' doKey, which is the method that turns Filter.Key into the query-string field term.

fix_sites.entry_point: VectorStore.similaritySearch(SearchRequest) and VectorStore.delete(Filter.Expression) on the Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and GemFire VectorStore implementations (all funnel through convertExpression -> doKey/doSingleValue -> emitLuceneString)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared core filter-converter library (spring-ai-vector-store), not a store module

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The escaper is a protected static helper inside the core spring-ai-vector-store module, not one of the three vector stores the advisory names, so a solver can decide the bug belongs in each store's doKey and patch three copies of the loop instead of the shared helper (leaving the value path on emitLuceneString open).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keys containing ordinary spaces, colons, quotes and dots must keep being escaped literally (not rejected and not quoted wholesale), and the literal 'metadata.' prefix plus the ':' separator must stay unescaped; a fix that validates identifier characters like the sibling stores do, or that escapes the dot in a dotted key path, breaks these expectations. Dotted-key expectation: vector-stores/spring-ai-opensearch-store/src/test/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/opensearch/OpenSearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverterTest.java:159

O6_input_shapes: whitespace characters in a Filter.Key: ES and OpenSearch escape the prefixed path 'metadata.' + key.trim(), GemFire escapes the bare trimmed key
the same helper also formats String values: double-quoted for Elasticsearch, unquoted for OpenSearch and GemFire
list-valued filters (IN/NIN) go through the same doSingleValue per element
keys that look quoted ("...", '...') are still escaped character by character, quotes included
the published fix's own tests exercise the key shape only; the value shape is covered only implicitly by the shared helper

O8_uncovered_routes.route: metadata filter keys (and unquoted OpenSearch/GemFire values) containing Unicode whitespace other than the four newly escaped characters, e.g. U+00A0, U+2003, U+2028, U+202F, still reach the query string through the same switch's default branch unescaped
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and its tests enumerate only tab, newline, carriage return and U+3000, and exotic Unicode spaces look like an edge case nobody asked about, so the list can be treated as complete.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same helper in the core module; one file from every store converter

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second escaping helper (e.g. emitLuceneText) used by one store converter for values while emitLuceneString is used for keys, so the same key/value can be escaped by two different character sets.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The three Lucene stores already duplicate their own value handling (Elasticsearch quotes, OpenSearch and GemFire do not), so a maintainer adding a fourth store or a quote-preserving variant would plausibly hand-roll a second loop rather than reuse the helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-store hand-written escape switch (as Redis already has for TAG values) added next to the shared Lucene helper for a store that needs its own character set.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Hand-rolled escape switches per store are the existing house style at this commit (Redis, Typesense, Azure and Weaviate each carry their own identifier rule), so a copy of the Lucene loop in a new store module is natural.

O9_family: CWE-943 improper neutralization of special elements in query logic (filter-expression / query-string injection)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (./mvnw wrapper available at repo root, maven-compiler-plugin 3.14.1, spring-javaformat plugin); large multi-module reactor (~178 poms)
O10_build.project_tests: Plain JUnit 5 converter unit tests that need no server: ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverterTest, OpenSearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverterTest, GemFireAiSearchFilterExpressionConverterTest; the *IT classes in the same modules need live Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/GemFire instances and are not needed for this behaviour.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the four characters to a switch inside each of the three store converters' doKey (or escape keys only), leaving the shared emitLuceneString and therefore every value path untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Nothing outside this advisory's protection was pursued; the other vector-store converters (Redis, Typesense, Azure, Weaviate) already carry their own identifier allowlists at this commit, and no change to them was contemplated.
unverified: repo_mb: repository size not measured (no shell in this session); the tree is a large multi-module reactor but well under 1.5 GB of source is assumed, not verified.

The claim that Lucene/Elasticsearch query_string treats U+00A0/U+2003/U+2028/U+202F as whitespace comes from the Lucene query-parser grammar and the ES reserved-characters documentation, not from anything in this tree, so the O8 route's exploitability is inferred rather than proven here.
present_in_latest is unknown because no latest-release code was supplied for this entry.

The O2 site is the same file the published fix changed: it is recorded as a lower_level_api/cause-layer site (a core-module shared helper reached by three named store modules), not as a leftover hole the fix ignored.
If O2 and O8 are discounted, the `single_site` red flag would hold instead: the source change is a single 4-case addition inside one switch in one function.
